correctness.rationale: The published Gauss-image criterion reduces X-raying a face to avoiding its Gauss image with an orthogonal great circle. Exact facet normals show that each icosahedral vertex lies in an open normal hemisphere selected by the coordinate axis of its golden-ratio coordinate. Signed-coordinate symmetry covers all twelve vertices, face Gauss images are contained in vertex Gauss images, and the universal lower bound X(K)>=3 gives equality. The bundled exact-arithmetic checker reconstructs all twenty facets and verifies every strict sign condition.

value.rationale: The regular icosahedron is a canonical Platonic solid and X-ray number is a classical convex-geometric invariant tied to illumination. The exact value reaches the universal three-dimensional lower bound despite a normal cone that lies outside the standard almost-smooth regime. The result gives an explicit optimal triple of directions and a useful benchmark for how far the almost-smooth hypothesis is from necessity.
